title: Ramayana Trailer Launches in Delhi to Industry Fanfare as Arun Govil Reveals He Plays Dashrath
excerpt: Nitesh Tiwari's two-part epic drew praise from across the film industry at a grand Delhi event, where the original TV Rama confirmed his return as Lord Ram's father and the music team of Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman shared behind-the-scenes stories.
body:
• Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana held a grand trailer launch in Delhi attended by Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Yash, Arun Govil, Karan Johar, and other Bollywood figures.
  • Arun Govil, who played Lord Rama in Ramanand Sagar's iconic 1987 TV serial, revealed he will play Maharaj Dashrath — Rama's father — in the new film.
  • The two-part saga features a score by Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman, with Shreya Ghoshal recording the Ram-Sita swayamvar song. Part 1 releases Diwali 2026.
  • Director Atlee called Ranbir Kapoor "stunning" and Yash "unbelievably lethal," while the official global trailer debut is set for San Diego Comic-Con on July 24.

A Star-Studded Delhi Event

The trailer for Ramayana: Part 1, one of the most anticipated Indian films in years, was unveiled at a grand event in Delhi over the weekend, drawing an A-list crowd and immediate industry praise. Producer Namit Malhotra, director Nitesh Tiwari, and stars Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, and Ravi Dubey were joined on stage by Yash, who plays Ravana, and a roster of Bollywood luminaries including Karan Johar, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, and Swami Ramdev.

The event, hosted by poet and lyricist Kumar Vishwas — who has served as a cultural consultant on the film — featured speeches, anecdotes, and the evening's biggest reveal.

Arun Govil Passes the Baton

Arun Govil, who defined Lord Rama for an entire generation through Ramanand Sagar's 1987 television serial, confirmed that he plays Maharaj Dashrath — Rama's father — in the new film. The casting represents a symbolic passing of the torch: the actor who once embodied Rama now plays the king who must send his son into exile.

"I used to think how I reacted when I saw the actor playing the same character I played at that time. I used to get this thought every time on the sets."

— Arun Govil, on watching Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama

Govil called the film one that "has put Indian cinema at par with Hollywood," praising both Malhotra and Tiwari as "wonderful human beings."

Music and Scale

Kumar Vishwas shared a behind-the-scenes story that drew laughter and applause. During the recording of the Ram-Sita swayamvar song — with A.R. Rahman, Hans Zimmer, and Shreya Ghoshal in the studio — Malhotra's wife arrived late at night. The team assumed she came to watch the session. Instead, she announced it was their wedding anniversary. "It's a different matter that the anniversary song was sung by the biggest singer of our time and the biggest musicians at present," Vishwas said.

The collaboration between Rahman and Zimmer — two of the most decorated film composers alive — signals the scale of the production. Malhotra noted that the team consulted 300 versions of the Ramayana across traditions to ensure cultural sensitivity, with Kumar Vishwas providing guidance on how to navigate differing interpretations.

Industry Reactions

Director Atlee, best known for Jawan with Shah Rukh Khan, took to social media shortly after the trailer screening. "Absolutely blown away by the Ramayana trailer! What a vision," he wrote, calling Yash "unbelievably lethal," Ranbir Kapoor "stunning," and Sai Pallavi "ethereal."

Yash, making a rare speech in Hindi, framed the project in broader cultural terms. "This is India's dream," he said. "We all have come together with one vision and one conviction — to put our story on the global platform."

Global Rollout Begins

Produced by Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios in association with DNEG and Yash's Monster Mind Creations, the film is planned as a two-part saga. Part 1 is scheduled for release during Diwali 2026, with Part 2 following in Diwali 2027. Both films will have a worldwide IMAX release.

The official global trailer debut is set for San Diego Comic-Con on July 24, where Malhotra, Tiwari, and the main cast will present a panel in Ballroom 20 — one of the most high-profile international platforms ever used for an Indian film launch. The SDCC premiere positions Ramayana not just as a domestic event film, but as a global cinematic spectacle aimed at audiences far beyond India.
image_caption: Ranbir Kapoor stars as Lord Rama in Nitesh Tiwari's two-part Ramayana saga. The film's Delhi trailer launch drew praise from across the Indian film industry.
nri_angle: The Ramayana adaptation is among the most-anticipated Indian films globally, with its Comic-Con debut and IMAX release directly targeting the diaspora audience.
